picks.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
picks.why_plausible: Identity-adjacent performance apparel buyer with low-medium price sensitivity who explicitly responds to technical fabrics and athlete endorsements — the patroller claim lands directly. AOV of $88 is far below $650, but this is the persona most likely to stretch for gear that signals serious athletic capability.
lean_into: performance claims
technical fabrics
pro/patroller endorsement as the athlete proof point
picks.ad_angle: The shell ski patrollers actually wear — built to perform, not to pose.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: price_sensitivity: low and a system-optimizer mindset that pays premiums for gear that measurably works; her fitness affinity extends naturally to backcountry touring, an endurance sport. The score undercounted her because outerwear isn't in her tag list, but she's the one persona who'll happily read the spec sheet.
lean_into: outcome-focused claims (stays dry, breathes on the skin track)
technical transparency about materials and construction
willingness to pay once for something that performs
avoid: vague 'premium' language with nothing behind it
picks.ad_angle: Gear as equipment: the measurable difference a real hardshell makes on a long day of touring.

picks.name: The Gifter
picks.why_plausible: The brief lists gift as an occasion at 0.5, and this persona has price_sensitivity: low with an apparel affinity and a stated appetite for 'impressive-looking' high-AOV purchases. A $650+ shell is the rare gift that reads as serious and unmistakably expensive.
lean_into: giftable, premium presentation
the patroller-grade story as something impressive to tell the recipient
shipping timing for a season-dated gift
avoid: dense technical jargon that a non-skier gifter can't evaluate
picks.ad_angle: The gift for the skier who already owns everything — patrol-grade, and they'd never buy it for themselves.

picks.name: The Affluent Classic
picks.why_plausible: price_sensitivity: low, typical_aov_usd: 145 (highest in the set), and she values quality and longevity over trends — a buy-once shell is exactly that argument. Her travel and classic_apparel affinities fit a mountain-trip buyer; the score docked her mainly on publisher reach, not on fit.
lean_into: craftsmanship and construction quality
understated, quality-focused tone
buy it once, keep it for a decade
picks.ad_angle: Built to outlast the trend cycle — one shell, made properly, for every winter to come.

campaign.name: Technical outerwear (hard shells) for backcountry skiing · post-purchase launch

bid_strategy.rationale: $750 first order × 0.30 = $225.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: Assumed a first order around $750 based on the $650 starting price.
Assumed the gear is sold to both men and women.
Assumed a one-time purchase rather than a subscription.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: 1 creative(s) failed review twice and are paused: The Affluent Classic.
No publisher in this catalog is a good fit; nothing would run.
